discrepancies.detail: PROTOCOL-ADDENDUM-rho-neg.md says 'The card records the source and binary sha256 in its receipt.' The card has no hashing command and receipt-n01.json has no binary digest (the binary was removed by remove-bin). The source is bound (card binds, clean tree at the run commit); binary identity rests on the command sequence of one card (build once, every run command invokes that path) and on the continuity controls, which reproduce the recorded rows. Same limitation as card-01.

discrepancies.what: plain rho is cheaper than rho-neg inside the band
discrepancies.detail: rho-neg cheaper at ['16 bits w=0', '16 bits w=0.1', '20 bits w=0', '24 bits w=0', '28 bits w=0']; plain rho cheaper at ['16 bits w=1', '20 bits w=0.1', '20 bits w=1', '24 bits w=0.1', '24 bits w=1', '28 bits w=0.1', '28 bits w=1']. rho-neg emits {16: 3.66, 20: 3.63, 24: 3.59, 28: 3.58} native operations per accepted step (dptest, canon, lookahead on negated candidates, cyctest) against about 1.1 for plain rho, each charged w GAE. The rho order therefore flips inside the band at every cell (unresolved at that boundary). The addendum foresaw this and fixed the rule (an order statement must hold against both rhos); arm (a)'s order holds against both. Not a defect; but S/rho-neg understates the distance to the cheapest measured rho wherever plain rho is cheaper (per_cell gap_S_over_cheaper_rho).

discrepancies.what: addendum expectation 'the gap is expected to shrink by about sqrt 2 at w = 0' is inverted
discrepancies.detail: a rho that is sqrt 2 cheaper makes S/rho grow by sqrt 2, not shrink. Measured at w = 0, S/rho-neg = (S/plain rho) x {16: 1.357, 20: 1.154, 24: 1.102, 28: 1.186} (plain/neg). The ratio is below sqrt 2 at 20-28 bits partly because the recorded plain-rho sample ran short (mean steps / sqrt(pi n/2) = {16: 1.195, 20: 0.823, 24: 0.823, 28: 0.928}) while rho-neg ran near expectation (mean steps / sqrt(pi n/4) = {16: 0.948, 20: 0.936, 24: 1.012, 28: 1.064}); independent 16-run samples, within sampling error. The other half of the expectation, gap above 1 at every cell and weight, holds (smallest S/rho-neg 6.497).

limitations: One curve per size and 16 logarithms per cell. The 95% t half-width of a cell mean reaches 34% for rho-neg and 33% for plain rho (largest over cells and w), 16% for arm (a). The order is robust to it: arm (a)'s lower 95% bound exceeds both rhos' upper 95% bounds at every cell and weight (per_cell ci95_separated_at_all_w).

The rho-neg vs plain rho comparison is between independent samples (distinct targets and walk seeds by design), not paired runs; per-cell plain/neg ratios carry about 11% (16 bits) to 20% (28 bits) relative standard error, from the per-run coefficients of variation.
Partition hashes (part(x) per step), coefficient updates mod n and Brent's saved-class copies are not counted on either rho, as in the original protocol; listed per AGENTS.md 5a.
theta = floor(bits/4) uses the cell label, as PROTOCOL.md does; the new walk inherits it unchanged.

rho-neg can solve inside a walk when a detected cycle closes with different coefficients (5 of the 64 measured runs ended that way, per the validator's port); plain rho has no cycle check. This is part of the addendum's specified fruitless-cycle handling and is counted, not an uncounted shortcut.
The receipt records no environment (rustc version, CPU for target-cpu=native) and no timestamps; counts do not depend on either, and wall time (ms) is not used.

The Python port was written after reading the instrument; it shows the rows follow from the code and the addendum's seed formulas, not that an independent reading of the addendum alone yields the same walk.
Validated content is snapshot 41155e5554; HEAD has since gained the replay lane's commits d63dea4372 and 043f1eb98c, which change none of the files read (each read file equals its snapshot blob).
This report makes no ECDLP claim and authorizes no promotion; it admits the rho-neg rows as the gate's matched rho reference for arm (a) at the four design cells.
